hook.text: A training dataset loses its license after models are already in production.
And how do you prove nothing was missed?

problem.text: Most catalogs can show lineage, but an incident still closes through screenshots, tickets, and memory.
RecallGraph turns that gap into a deterministic model recall command: trace every affected descendant, require human dispositions, and fail closed until the evidence is complete.

impact.text: This case starts with a revoked source.
The normalized graph reaches two models and one production deployment.
Both model decisions are unresolved, so closure and writeback are blocked.
The hosted console is clearly labeled fixture evidence; the workflow is deterministic and repeatable for every judge.

govern.text: RecallGraph binds each approval to the current case revision, so changed evidence makes stale approvals invalid.
After both reviewed dispositions are recorded, a server-issued writeback reference unlocks the guarded close action.

receipt.text: Closing the case exports the complete lineage, event, decisions, approvals, uncertainty resolutions, and writeback evidence as canonical JSON.
SHA-256 produces a stable integrity digest.
Plant one mismatch, and verification fails without pretending the checksum is a signature.

datahub.text: The sponsor integration is real and separate from the hosted fixture.
Against DataHub OSS, mcp-server-datahub returned two affected ML models and one downstream process.
RecallGraph then wrote a probe metadata property, confirmed readback, and restored the original value.
The retained evidence records every URN.

close.text: RecallGraph is public under Apache 2.0, deployed on Vercel, and covered by one hundred automated checks plus a green production build.
Every affected model, traced and resolved.
Open the live recall command or inspect the repository.
